title: Driving two regions together or apart
paper: Gifford, Jastrzębowska, Singer and Cichy 2025, Nature Human Behaviour

steps.title: Screen in the model
steps.paper: Encoding models predicted responses of two visual areas to all 73,000 images of the Natural Scenes Dataset, far more than were shown in the scanner.
steps.here: Every stimulus rendered on the counter so far, read by TRIBE in early visual cortex and the lateral occipital region.

steps.title: Align and disentangle
steps.paper: Images were selected that drive both areas up or down together, or one up while the other goes down.
steps.here: The five stimuli that best meet each condition, with each region's readouts put on a common scale.

steps.title: Against a baseline
steps.paper: Each condition was tested against images chosen without optimisation.
steps.here: Each condition against 10,000 random sets of five.

steps.title: Validate on new data
steps.paper: The selected images were shown to new participants in a new fMRI experiment.
steps.here: TRIBE has one average viewer, so new data means a view the screen never saw: the selected stimuli rendered again from a 40 degree camera angle.

args.title: Selected stimuli from a new camera angle

bindings.a: a stimulus selected to drive both regions

steps.title: Hand off
steps.paper: The relationships found in the model were then checked in people's brains.
steps.here: The selected stimuli, their predicted effects and the validation run go into the hand-off bundle.
